sections.h2: What are the selling options in Tonawanda?
sections.html:
This page covers the town in Erie County that wraps around the Village of Kenmore, sometimes called Ken-Ton. The city of the same name sits north along the canal and is a different municipality, so confirm which one holds your parcel before you begin. Owners usually weigh an ordinary listing against an all-cash purchase by a direct buyer.

Listing fits a house in show condition when you can sit through a mortgage approval. A direct sale fits when repairs have piled up, a job is moving you out of the area, or an estate has several heirs to coordinate. Compare the net from each path, since the easy route and the profitable route are sometimes different.

  • Agent listing: the most exposure, plus staging, showings and a closing tied to the buyer's bank.
  • Do-it-yourself sale: you price it, host the visits and negotiate the contract.
  • All-cash purchase: no bank involved, with the house accepted as you leave it.

Each path hits one local requirement, a storm water certificate, which is explained further down.

sections.h2: What is it like to own a home in Tonawanda?
sections.html:
Tonawanda is Buffalo's northern inner-ring suburb. Census estimates list 70,853 residents for mid-2025 (QuickFacts), and 33,965 households were counted in the 2020 to 2024 survey. Its 18.7 square miles of land run from the Niagara River in the west to Niagara Falls Boulevard, which is US 62, in the east.

Settlers arrived around 1805, and the Erie Canal, finished in 1825, sped things along. The town split from Buffalo in 1836, Kenmore incorporated in 1899, and a big wave of suburban building followed in the 1940s and 1950s. Population peaked at 107,282 in 1970 and has eased since, which tells you much of the stock is from that era.

Roads are an asset. Interstate 190 runs down the western side, Interstate 290 crosses to US 62, and state routes 324, 265, 266 and 384 serve the neighborhoods in between. Workers average a 20.6 minute trip. Names buyers know include Brighton, Kenilworth, Parkview, Sheridan Parkside, Green Acres and Old Town, plus Ellicott Creek Park and the Sheridan and Brighton Park golf courses.

sections.h2: What do ownership and price figures show for Tonawanda?
sections.html:
A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $213,900 here, and owners live in 72.2 percent of the homes. Median household income is $77,673, and about one resident in five has passed 65.

Few people move in a given year, with 90.2 percent staying put. Monthly owner costs run $1,494 with a mortgage and $662 without. Buyers will compare your house with other 1950s-era suburban homes, so condition and updates carry weight.

Schools are a selling point. Kenmore-Tonawanda Union Free School District serves most of the area and runs Kenmore West and Kenmore East high schools, while Sweet Home Central covers a smaller portion. Verify which one serves your street before you name it in an ad.

sections.h2: What is the storm water certificate for a Tonawanda sale?
sections.html:
The town's I Want To page answers a common seller question: yes, you need a certificate of compliance covering the storm water system before the sale. The Building Department arranges the inspection at (716) 877-8801, and it looks at several parts of the system.

  • The sump pump and the electric line that powers it
  • Footing drains
  • Yard drains
  • Downspouts

Book it before you list. A dead pump or a misdirected downspout takes time to fix, and the week before closing is a poor time to learn about it. The page also says permit documents from before 1965 were destroyed, so hold on to your own receipts for older work.

Two town programs may also come up. A 0% Residential Rehabilitation loan secured by a mortgage on your house comes due when title transfers. The First Time Homebuyer Program was permanently suspended on March 31, 2025, so a buyer cannot count on it for closing costs.

sections.h2: How do Tonawanda tax bills and assessment appeals work?
sections.html:
Per the assessor's page, the office values 28,828 parcels in the town and Kenmore, worth $10.9 billion in market value. Exemption filings and status are fixed on March 1, the tentative roll appears May 1, and the final roll is filed by July 1.

Ask the receiver of taxes at the Town Clerk to confirm the dates and amounts on your own bill, because the schedule is reset yearly.

  • Informal review: from February 1 to April 1, email evidence of your home's value to the assessor.
  • Grievance Day: the Board of Assessment Review sits on the fourth Tuesday of May (May 25, 2027) and takes form RP-524. You may submit in writing and skip the hearing.
  • Small Claims Assessment Review: a court-run next step for an owner-occupied home of up to three families, with a $30 fee and petitions due by July 30.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and recent changes matter to Tonawanda owners?
sections.html:
Owner-occupied houses are eligible for STAR, though the state runs the program and the assessor has no power over a STAR record. If your benefit changed from a bill exemption to a credit check, let your mortgage servicer know so any escrow account is adjusted.

Other exemptions on the town's list cover seniors, disabled residents, veterans, firefighters and volunteer ambulance workers. The town adopted a full exemption for permanently and totally disabled veterans as of July 2026, and applications go to the assessor by March 1, 2027.

You can pay a tax bill on the town's online portal. Partial payments are different: those are taken only in person at the Town Clerk's office on weekdays, 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM.

sections.h2: What should a Tonawanda seller do about water, trash and the yard?
sections.html:
The town's Water Billing Department, at 716-871-8843, can stop or start service and set up a final bill, so call it once you have a closing date. Plumbing from the water meter into the house, including the meter, belongs to the homeowner. A leaky outdoor spigot or a running toilet can inflate a bill, which is worth fixing before a buyer reads your water history.

Town crews collect old paint, concrete from a homeowner's own project, bundled branches no longer than six feet and refrigerators with the doors removed, as the same page explains. Tires go to the Highway Department at 450 Woodward Avenue in Kenmore. Clearing the garage before the inspection and showings is easier when you know what the town will take on your regular garbage day.

Keep the lawn in order too. The town says grass and weeds should not pass 10 inches, and a Code Enforcement Officer can fine an owner who does not cut after a 10-day notice. A vacant house with a tall lawn invites complaints, so arrange mowing if you move out before the sale closes.

faqs.q: Is a sump pump inspection really required to sell here?
faqs.a: Yes. The town requires a storm water certificate of compliance for a sale, and the check includes the pump, its power line and the drains and downspouts. The Building Department books it at (716) 877-8801.

faqs.q: Is the city of Tonawanda included here?
faqs.a: No. These notes are for the town around Kenmore. The city is a separate municipality along the canal to the north, so ask that city's offices about its rules.

faqs.q: When can I contest my assessment in person?
faqs.a: Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday of May, which lands on May 25 in 2027. File RP-524 with the assessor and attach comparable sales if you have them.

faqs.q: What happens to a town rehab loan when I sell?
faqs.a: The deferred loan falls due when title transfers. The town's description lists a sale, any change in who is on the deed, a home equity loan and moving out as triggers, so ask the Community Development office for a payoff figure.

faqs.q: How quickly can an all-cash sale close here?
faqs.a: The date depends on the buyer and the title search, so have it put in writing. The storm water certificate and any open tax balance are the likeliest items to move it.
